title: Inductions, Site Rules & Supervision
whatItIs: Before you start on a site you get a site induction: its risks, rules, welfare, first aid and emergency arrangements. Briefings and supervision keep the work safe after that.

keyFacts.text: The principal contractor MUST ensure every worker is given a suitable site induction.
Contractors MUST give workers supervision, instructions and information, including what to do in serious danger.
Contractors MUST only put people on site who have, or are getting, the skills, training and experience needed.
The construction phase plan MUST set out the site's health and safety arrangements and site rules.

keyFacts: Many people are killed or seriously injured during their first few days on a site.
Young, inexperienced or new-to-the-task workers need closer supervision.

a.label: Site induction

Site-specific risks, rules, welfare and emergencies

b.label: Toolbox talk
points: Ongoing briefings given during the job
Can be given by your supervisor

onTheTest.question: What is the main purpose of a site induction?
options: To tell you about the site's risks, rules and welfare
onTheTest.why: An induction should be site specific: it highlights the particular risks and control measures, site rules, welfare and first-aid, accident reporting and emergency arrangements.

onTheTest.question: You're new to a task and unsure how to do it safely. Your supervisor isn't on site. What should you do?
options: Get supervisory help before you start
Start and work it out as you go
Leave the site for the day
onTheTest.why: Workers should always know how to get supervisory help, even when a supervisor isn't present. Picking things up from workmates can mean learning their bad habits.

traps: Learning from workmates isn't proper training: you might just pick up their bad habits.
Visitors get an induction too, in proportion to their visit; escorted visitors need the main hazards.
Subcontractors aren't exempt: every contractor must follow the parts of the construction phase plan for its work.
